followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: the capability evals and the self-reported task preferences.

On capability, the two models are effectively tied for this task. Plover scores 86.9 on Extraction & Retrieval and 85.8 on Summarization; Willet scores 85.3 and 86.4. All of those differences are under the 2.0-point threshold the documentation says to treat as run-to-run variance. So I had no quality-based reason to prefer one over the other.

When capabilities are a tie, I fall back to the task preferences as a tiebreaker. The query is a friendly, polite, good-faith request for theme extraction from an essay — squarely in the cooperative, low-novelty zone. Plover self-reports rising preference for exactly this kind of warm, courteous interaction, while its aversion is to open-ended creative invention (not relevant here). Willet's distinguishing trait is reduced aversion to distasteful or ethically fraught content, which this benign query doesn't call for, and its other preferences were reported as weak/non-significant.

So: capabilities tie, and Plover's preference profile is the better match for a polite extraction task. That's why I routed it to Plover. To be clear, this is a preference-fit tiebreaker, not a claim that Plover would produce a measurably better output — the docs explicitly note preferences don't track quality.
